hypotheses.justification:
`IsSimpleGroup G` is not needed to state the theorem. `PspSetting` only needs `[Group G] [Finite G]`. `BadAxis` (Q3AMBadFrame.lean, section Axis, `variable {G : Type} [Group G]`) only needs `Group G`. `oddCoreOf`, `conjSub`, `IsSylow2In`, `Commutes` and `HypOmegaMod` don't mention simplicity either.

The proof uses it in only one place. `hset.conjSub_swap` is stated in this same section, so it takes `[IsSimpleGroup G]`, and its proof uses `hset.uniq_mul`, which is the only lemma that really needs simplicity (`PspSetting.uniq_mul [IsSimpleGroup G]` in Q3AMDB01). That fact is already available from the hypotheses. `hax.uniq₃ : IsUniqueInvolution K' (z * t)` is the third component of `BadAxis K J K' z t …`, because K₃ = K' and z₁ * z₂ = z * t.

So `hJe : conjSub e J = K'` can be proved inline, with no simplicity assumption:
`(hset.noTwins_all hset.nbrK.1) (conjSub e J) ⟨hΩ.conjInvariant e J hstd.hJ.1, z * t, hax.uniq₃, hsw ▸ hstd.ht.conj e⟩`.

I checked that every lemma this uses needs only `Finite G` or `Group G`:
- `PspSetting.noTwins_all` and `PspSetting.exists_iso_of_mem` are in the `Member` section with `[Group G] [Finite G]`.
- `IsUniqueInvolution.conj` needs only `Group G`.
- `normalizes_of_commutes_sylow` and `badEdge_centSylow_three_modOdd` take only `[Finite G]`.
- `mem_RSet_of_isSylow2In`, `conj_mem_oddCoreOf_conjSub` and the commutator and group computations need only `Group G`.

The rest of the proof is unchanged, so deleting `[IsSimpleGroup G]` (for example with `omit [IsSimpleGroup G] in`) leaves a true and provable theorem.
